items.snippet: The Fairmont Le Château Frontenac, a hotel built by the Canadian Pacific Railway company in 1893, is Quebec City’s center of orbit.

Roam the cobblestone streets of Le Quartier Petit Champlain, a historic commercial district in Old Quebec, a neighborhood in Quebec City, founded in 1608 by the French explorer Samuel de Champlain. Old Quebec toggles two terrains: a lower town at sea level, and an upper town on t
The Morrin Center, the site of a former jailhouse, is now home to a library with an expansive English-language book collection.
Montmorency Falls, a roughly 15-minute drive east of Quebec, is a 272-foot-tall waterfall with several vantage points, including an observation deck and a suspension bridge.

items.place: Musée National des Beaux-Arts du Québec
items.snippet: Quebec City’s largest art museum, the Musée National des Beaux-Arts du Québec, will until late April host a touring art collection called “Early Days,” featuring works by Indigenous artists.
Skate at Place D’Youville, the public square near the festively decorated St.-Jean gate, one of the entryways into the old city.
For the first time, the Old Port of Quebec is hosting Discoglace, an outdoor rink that comes alive at night.
Speed down a toboggan track at Au 1884, the slide near Château Frontenac.
The Hôtel de Glace, an ice hotel about 35 minutes northwest of Quebec City, is celebrating its 25th anniversary this year.
Le Café du Monde has been around for more than 37 years and serves up classic Parisian fare.
Laurie Raphaël is an upscale restaurant that offers a tasting menu, with the option to add a wine or alcohol-free cocktail pairing. It also runs Lueur, a 14-seat, countertop dining experience.

Bar Ste-Angèle is a rustic jazz club behind a nondescript blue door on the hilly Rue Ste.-Angele. Another venue featuring daily live music is Pub Saint-Alexandre.

At La Buche, Quebecois dishes shine, from classics like tourtière (meat pie) and poutine (French fries and cheese curds topped with gravy), to meals using local ingredients like bison filet mignon and trout gravlax smoked over maple wood.
Café Apotek, simply furnished in an ode to Danish contemporary design, serves up canelés, sweet buns loaded with flavored mascarpone cream, and weighs espresso shots for an even latte pull each time.
Hono Izakaya is a Japanese restaurant that serves tapas-style plates next door to its sibling restaurant, Hono Ramen, which specializes in the brothy Japanese noodle dish.

Les Antiquités Bolduc is operated by a brother-sister duo who inherited the business from their parents and have curated a unique collection of items, from porcelain dishes and glass paperweights to vintage cameras, all beautifully displayed.

items.place: Oh La La! Boutique Éco Chic
items.snippet: Oh La La! Boutique Éco Chic is a vintage clothing shop specializing in luxury and designer items.
Rosie Papeterie, the Quebec stationary shop, was previously available only online but recently opened its first boutique, which also carries items like jewelry and fragrances from local creators.

The dozens of auberges, or inns, you’ll see dotting the streets fall into roughly two categories: hostels or boutique hotels. For the latter, Auberge Saint Antoine, a hotel near the Old Port of Quebec on the St. Lawrence River, offers a luxury experience starting at 230 dollars a

Quiet fills the air at Le Monastère des Augustines, a former monastery in Old Quebec that was converted in 2015 to a nonprofit wellness hotel. Guests have the option of sleeping in the sparsely furnished but comfortable nuns’ quarters, which start at around 200 dollars per night.

Vacation rentals are available on platforms like AirBnb and Vrbo. Look for options in the Saint-Roch neighborhood, where you’ll find many of the city’s best restaurants and nightlife, and an easy walk to major attractions.
